new_statements.quote: III.—Accent. In the Dafla language accent does not apparently play so important a part as in Miri. The accent usually falls on the penultimate syllable of a word, but in delivering a sentence the position of a word in such sentence may cause it to change its accent or even to change its vowels from long to short or vice versâ, in order to suit the cadence of the sentence, e.g., Iki mûllûngâ chê-û-sû-dna. ... The dogs are fighting. but— Lûpâ au-nâm iki-a si. ... This is the dog that was shot in the neck. In the former sentence 'iki' is rather slurred over, but in the latter it is the most important word, and a slight pause takes place before pronouncing it, which has the effect of lengthening the first vowel and shortening the second.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent, said to be weak in Dafla, usually falls on the penultimate syllable of the word (no weight condition stated); in connected speech a word's position/prominence in the sentence can shift the accent and lengthen or shorten its vowels.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged 'usually'; accent 'does not apparently play so important a part'; sentence cadence/focus overrides word accent (iki example). Modern sources (CIIL LIS-India; Rimum 2021; Ganu 2026; Murtem 2025) describe Nyishi as a three-tone language (rising/level/falling) and say nothing about stress; Chhangte 1992 via Sun 1993/Namkung 1996 p.296 mentions vowel neutralization 'in unstressed syllables' and length contrast only in first syllables, without a placement rule; Post 2015 reports conflicting evidence on Nyishi tone.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level default explicitly contrasted by Hamilton with sentence-level cadence; examples are sentences, rule stated for 'a word'. Variety: 'Eastern Dafla'/Nyisu, Lower Subansiri Nyishi north of North Lakhimpur (Namkung 1996 p.296) = nyis1236.
new_statements.identity_note: nisi1239 is a Glottolog BOOKKEEPING languoid ('Dafla', family 'Bookkeeping') created for the retired ISO 639-3 code [dap] 'Nisi/Nishi', which ISO split in 2012 (CR 2011-132) into Nyishi [njz] (Glottolog nyis1236 'Nyishi-Hill Miri') and Tagin [tgj] (tagi1241). It is not a distinct language. The only first-hand accent statement found (Hamilton 1900, 'Dafla as spoken by the tribes immediately south of the Apa Tanang country' = Lower Subansiri / 'Eastern Dafla' Nyishi per Namkung 1996 p.296) is the SAME passage already coded in the catalog under nyis1236 (verdict QI-FIXED, adjudicated A/B/C 2026-09-12). Adding nisi1239 would double-count one language (retired codes confer no identity); it should be recorded as duplicate_of nyis1236, not as a new catalog entry. Tagin (tagi1241) has its own audit folder and no stress statement.
